thread.title: 10-Treasury yield extends fall to January low amid China growth fears

author: Sunny Oh
title: 10-Treasury yield extends fall to January low amid China growth fears
text:
Treasury prices rose Thursday, and yields retreated, after Apple trimmed its sales guidance, heightening concerns around the health of China, the second-largest economy in the world.
The 10-year Treasury note yield TMUBMUSD10Y, +0.98% fell 2.1 basis points to 2.640%, its lowest since January. The 2-year note yield TMUBMUSD02Y, +0.49% was down 1.4 basis points to 2.490%, while the 30-year bond yield TMUBMUSD30Y, +0.56% slipped 2.4 basis points to 2.958%, its lowest since July. Bond prices move in the opposite direction of yields.
Anxieties around China’s economic slowdown remained on investors’ agenda after Apple Inc. AAPL, +0.11% said it expected revenues to fall below forecasts, citing slower-than-expected growth in China. U.S. equities were poised to open lower, with futures for the Dow Jones Industrial Average YMH9, -1.14% and Nasdaq-100 NQH9, -1.77% down sharply. The dour investor sentiment spurred inflows into haven assets like government paper and the Japanese yen.
Meanwhile, Dallas Fed President Robert Kaplan said Thursday morning that the selloff in financial markets has caused him to support a pause in further interest-rate hikes until the uncertainties settle. In an interview with Bloomberg News, Kaplan said the Fed should remain on the sidelines at least for the “first couple of quarters” of the year.
Adding to the stock-market jitters, the government shutdown shows no signs of coming to an end, postponing the releases of economic data. However, the Bureau of Labor Statistic will still issue employment reports.

Nevertheless, investors have plenty of economic data to digest. The ADP employment report for December will come out at 8:15 a.m. Eastern, followed by jobless claims for the week ending in Dec. 29 at 8:30 a.m.
More important, investors will pore over the Institute of Supply Management’s manufacturing index for December. Economists polled by MarketWatch expect the index to fall to 57.0% from 59.3%, reflecting the broad-based weakness in the Federal Reserve’s regional surveys of factory activity.
“Following the drop in China’s [purchasing managers index] below 50, there is concern that tomorrow’s ISM factory index could post a sharper-than-expected drop. That concern has been stoked by the fact that all seven regional factory gauges released in December posted declines,” said Omair Sharif, senior U.S. economist for Société Générale, in a note.
